text: I'll start with the paged namespace's Service and the catalog deployment.

arguments.root_cause_statement: Service shop/catalog selects pods with the label app=catalog-api, but the pods produced by Deployment shop/catalog carry the label app=catalog (the deployment's pod template sets metadata.labels app=catalog). No pod in the namespace carries app=catalog-api, so the endpoint controller populated no addresses: Endpoints shop/catalog has no subsets and the overview shows endpointAddresses=0. Because Service ClusterIP 10.96.96.22 has no backends, connections from Deployment shop/storefront-gateway to the catalog backend never reach a pod, and the gateway logs "gateway: catalog fetch FAILED (timeout or connection refused)" on every poll, which is what the storefront sees as spinner hangs and empty product grids. The catalog pods themselves are healthy and serving, so the fix is to correct the Service selector back to app=catalog.
arguments.mechanism: Service shop/catalog has .spec.selector set to {app: catalog-api}, while the pods it is meant to front are labelled {app: catalog}; no pod in shop matches app=catalog-api, so the endpoint controller writes Endpoints shop/catalog with no subsets (endpointAddresses=0) and every TCP connection to ClusterIP 10.96.96.22:8080 has no backend to be forwarded to.

evidence.claim: The paged Service has zero endpoint addresses although both catalog pods are Running and Ready.
The storefront gateway's calls to the catalog backend do not complete.
evidence.quote: gateway: catalog fetch FAILED (timeout or connection refused)

evidence.claim: Deployment shop/catalog labels its pods app=catalog, which does not match the Service selector.
Endpoints shop/catalog contains no subsets at all.
The catalog container is actually listening on port 8080, so the backend itself is not the failure.

ruled_out.alternative: The catalog pods are unhealthy or not serving, so no ready backends exist.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: Both catalog pods are Running with the api container ready and zero restarts, and the container logs show it listening on 8080.

ruled_out.alternative: The gateway is pointed at a different or non-existent Service name.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: Only one Service exists in namespace shop, catalog on port 8080, so the gateway's catalog calls can only target it.

ruled_out.alternative: The Service port or targetPort is wrong (8080 mismatch with the container port).
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The Service targets port 8080 and the catalog container declares containerPort 8080, so the port mapping is correct.

verification.command: kubectl -n shop get service catalog -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'
kubectl -n shop get endpoints catalog -o yaml
